explanation: Matches Pommerenke's example on erdosproblems.com/1047. For f = z^k(z-a) the nonzero critical point is ka/(k+1), and its critical value is k^k a^{k+1}/(k+1)^{k+1}. That value equals 1 exactly at a0 = (1+1/k)k^{1/(k+1)}, and it exceeds 1 (so {|f| ≤ 1} splits into two components) only for a > a0. Taking real a in the one-sided interval (a0, a0+δ) is therefore the correct reading of 'sufficiently close'. The statement asserts two components and a non-convex component containing 0, for all large k.
